title: Why Compliance and Age Verification Are the Next Frontier of Frictionless Commerce
summary: As convenience and fuel retail becomes increasingly digital, compliance can no longer remain a manual exception within the customer journey. Retailers need age assurance solutions that integrate directly into checkout workflows.
body_markdown:
*How can convenience retailers create a more seamless customer experience while maintaining compliance?*


‍


## Direct Answer


As convenience and fuel retail becomes increasingly digital, compliance can no longer remain a manual exception within the customer journey. Retailers need age assurance solutions that integrate directly into checkout workflows. Not only does this help associates verify eligibility faster, it does so consistently and securely. By combining industry collaboration, integrated technology and privacy-first design, retailers can reduce friction at the point of sale (POS) while maintaining confidence in responsible retailing.


‍


## Key Takeaways


- Age-restricted categories continue to play a significant role in convenience retail,[accounting for 34% of inside sales in 2024](https://www.nacsmagazine.com/Issues/April-2025/The-Increased-Importance-of-OTP-Sales-in-C-Stores) .
- As retailers digitize payments, loyalty and checkout experiences, age verification remains one of the last major sources of friction in the customer journey.
- Industry collaboration is helping establish a more consistent approach to age assurance across convenience retail.
- Integrated age verification solutions can help reduce checkout friction while supporting compliance objectives.
- The future of frictionless commerce depends on balancing convenience, compliance and customer privacy.


‍


## The Customer Journey Has Gone Digital. Compliance Is the Next Opportunity.


Over the past decade, convenience and fuel retailers have transformed the customer experience. Mobile payments, digital loyalty programs, personalized offers and increasingly connected store operations have reshaped expectations. Consumers have grown accustomed to experiences that are fast, intuitive and consistent. Retailers, in turn, have invested in technologies that remove friction from nearly every stage of the shopping journey.


Yet one important interaction often remains disconnected from these modernization efforts: age verification.


This matters because age-restricted product categories remain a major part of convenience retail. According to NACS,[cigarettes and other tobacco products accounted for 34% of inside sales in convenience stores in 2024](https://www.nacsmagazine.com/Issues/April-2025/The-Increased-Importance-of-OTP-Sales-in-C-Stores) . That’s just one category of age-restricted products retailers have to consider. In fact, for most retailers, age assurance is not an edge case. It is a routine part of daily operations.


So as the rest of the retail experience becomes more digital, one question is becoming increasingly important:


**How can retailers create faster, more consistent customer experiences while maintaining confidence in compliance?**


Retailers have spent years standardizing and streamlining other parts of the customer journey. Compliance should be no different. Creating a common approach to age verification helps reduce friction for store associates, creates greater consistency for consumers and makes adoption easier for retailers.


> “TruAge was built by the industry because the industry believed age assurance was too important to leave to chance—or outside commercial interests.” - **Stephanie Sikorski, CEO of TruAge and Vice President of Strategic Initiatives at NACS**


That perspective highlights a growing reality for the industry: compliance is no longer separate from customer experience. It is an essential part of it.


‍


## Why Industry Collaboration Matters for Digital Age Assurance


Retail innovation rarely happens in isolation. Many of the experiences consumers now take for granted are possible because retailers, technology providers and industry organizations worked together to establish common approaches and broader accessibility.


Age assurance is increasingly following that path. As the industry looks to reduce friction while maintaining responsible retailing practices, collaboration has become essential. A fragmented approach creates inconsistency for retailers, associates and consumers alike. A shared framework creates opportunities to scale best practices more effectively.


This is why the ongoing work of organizations such as NACS and Conexxus is so important. Age assurance is a challenge that extends across the industry, making collaboration a critical part of the solution.


The goal is larger than technology adoption alone. It is about creating a more consistent experience wherever age-restricted products are sold.


‍


## Compliance Should Be Built Into the Workflow


If frictionless commerce is the goal, compliance must become part of the workflow rather than a process that sits outside it.


Retail associates already manage a wide range of responsibilities throughout every transaction. Asking them to move between disconnected systems or additional manual processes can introduce unnecessary complexity.


Integrated age assurance offers a different approach. Rather than treating compliance as a separate task, retailers can bring age verification directly into existing checkout workflows, helping create more consistent experiences for store teams and customers.


That philosophy is reflected in the recently announced collaboration between NCR Voyix and NACS to integrate the TruAge digital age-verification solution across NCR Voyix POS technology in the United States.


> “The NCR Voyix integration expands retailer access to TruAge and helps create the consistency, scale and interoperability needed for age assurance to work across the marketplace. This industry-led collaboration strengthens responsible retailing, prevents underage access and ensures convenience retailers help shape the future of age assurance.” - **Frank Gleeson, CEO of NACS**


For existing NCR Voyix RPOS customers, the certified TruAge solution is available through an API integration from Cullinan Group. Voyix POS for CFR includes native support for TruAge, giving retailers a path to add digital age assurance through the point-of-sale technology they already use.


The significance extends well beyond a single integration. It reflects a broader shift occurring across convenience retail as operators look to embed compliance into the same digital ecosystems that already support payments, loyalty and store operations.


When compliance becomes part of the transaction flow instead of an exception to it, retailers are better positioned to create experiences that feel both seamless and responsible.


‍


## The Future of Frictionless Commerce Must Also Protect Privacy


Modernizing compliance is not simply about speed. It is also about trust. As retailers adopt more digital solutions, consumers increasingly expect their personal information to be handled responsibly. Age verification should not require customers to reveal more information than necessary.


This is where privacy becomes an essential part of the frictionless commerce conversation.


According to TruAge, some traditional license-scanning approaches can expose more than[33 pieces of personally identifiable information](https://www.mytruage.org/about/faq) . By contrast, the TruAge process uses only four data points required to verify age and converts those data points into an anonymized token.


The result is a fundamentally different approach to compliance. Instead of revealing a consumer's identity in order to verify eligibility, retailers can focus on verifying only what is necessary.


The efficiency benefits are meaningful as well. TruAge reports that its age verification process can be up to[30 times faster than manual carding](https://www.mytruage.org/for-individuals) . That combination of convenience, compliance and privacy points toward a new principle for frictionless commerce: **verify age, not identity** .


As customer expectations continue to evolve, trust will increasingly be defined not only by what retailers protect, but also by what they choose not to collect in the first place.


‍


## Frictionless Commerce Means Every Step


Retailers have invested significant time and money into creating more convenient experiences across payments, loyalty, ordering and checkout. The next frontier is ensuring compliance evolves alongside them.


Age verification remains one of the most important interactions in convenience retail, particularly when age-restricted categories continue to represent a substantial share of store sales.


The future of compliance involves more than making the process faster. It’s about creating a more consistent, more scalable, and more privacy-conscious experience for the consumer.


By bringing age assurance into the broader frictionless commerce journey, retailers can help create experiences that support responsible retailing while meeting the expectations of modern consumers. Because in today's retail environment, frictionless commerce should extend to every step of the transaction, including compliance.


‍


#### Frequently Asked Questions


**What is frictionless compliance in retail?**


Frictionless compliance refers to technologies and processes that help retailers meet regulatory requirements while minimizing disruption to the customer experience.


**Why is age verification important in convenience retail?**


Age verification helps retailers comply with regulations governing age-restricted products while supporting responsible retailing practices. These categories continue to represent a significant portion of convenience store sales.


**How can retailers improve the age verification experience?**


Retailers can improve age verification by integrating digital age assurance solutions directly into existing checkout workflows, helping create faster and more consistent customer interactions.


**Can retailers improve compliance without sacrificing customer experience?**


Yes. Modern age assurance technologies are designed to support compliance while reducing operational friction for both customers and store associates.


**How does privacy fit into digital age verification?**


Privacy-first age assurance solutions can verify eligibility while minimizing the collection and exposure of personal information. TruAge, for example, uses only four data points required to verify age and converts them into an anonymized token.


**What role does industry collaboration play in age assurance?**


Industry collaboration helps create consistent approaches that are easier for retailers to adopt and scale, supporting both compliance and customer experience goals.
